title: Offer → First Release: 14d Activation & Support Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a tactical playbook for moving a newly accepted candidate from offer-acceptance to their first product-facing release within 14 days. Focus: minimize cognitive load, remove blocking access, and guarantee one small, end-to-end release they can own.

Audience:
People Ops (onboard ops), hiring manager, tech lead, assigned mentor/buddy, infra/SRE oncall for week-1.

High-level goals (success criteria):
- New hire has dev environment, repo access, and CI pipeline green by day 3.
- New hire lands a scoped change (bug fix, small feature) merged and shipped to staging by day 10 and prod within day 14.
- Post-release retro completed and signals captured (quality, ramp blockers, docs).

Quick timeline (14d sprint):
- Pre-start (offer accepted, 0 days): 
  - HR sends welcome packet & hardware form (IT ticket auto-created).
  - Manager assigns buddy & creates a tiny first-release ticket (<= 2 story points).
  - People Ops schedules orientation + security briefing.

- Day 0 (first day): 
  - 09:00 — Welcome + intro with manager (30m).
  - 10:00 — People Ops orientation (benefits, payroll, security basics) (45m).
  - 11:00 — Mentor pairing + team intro (30m).
  - Afternoon — Hardware delivered/checked in; quick access sweep (okta, corp VPN, GH, internal wiki).
  - TODO: Confirm CI read-only access and sandbox project.

- Days 1–3: bootstrapping 
  - Setup: repo clone, run local dev server, run tests.
  - Shadow: 1–2 pairing sessions with mentor on the target repo.
  - Small green ticket: reproduce a flaky test or fix a doc/typo in the codebase to validate commit flow.
  - People Ops check-in end of day 3 (async): did you get SSH keys, KMS requests, cloud role?

- Days 4–7: ownership starts 
  - New hire takes the scoped ticket from triage -> implement -> PR.
  - Manager/tech lead performs focused code review targeting correctness and learnability (not style nit-picks).
  - Mentor runs a dedicated testing session: how to run E2E locally, run canary.
  - Safety: infra validates feature flag gating and rollback path documented in PR template.

- Days 8–10: staging release 
  - Merge to main/staging per the team's established flow.
  - QA smoke test checklist executed by buddy/QA.
  - Observability: add a simple trace/log line and confirm metrics surface in console.
  - If rollout is complex, use phased canary (10% → 100%) — SRE to assist.

- Days 11–14: production release & retro 
  - Prod release with oncall & owner monitoring for first 4 hours.
  - Post-release retro within 48 hours: capture blockers, docs gaps, access friction.
  - People Ops 14-day pulse survey + 1:1 with manager scheduled.

Minimum checklist items (pre-merge & pre-prod gating):
- Access: GH, CI, staging infra creds, cloud project viewer/assume-role, secret access (KMS) approved.
- Security: completed secure-coding short checklist; dependency scan on PR.
- Observability: basic logs + alert threshold documented; dev added to alert recipient list for first 72h.
- Rollback: clear revert plan in PR + owner who can revert.
- Testing: unit tests added/updated; smoke script for staging run locally.

Interview rubric (kept short — template for future hires):
- Technical (score 1–5): problem decomposition, testability, reading existing code, small-system debugging.
- System judgment (1–5): release thinking, rollout/rollback, observability choices.
- Collaboration (1–5): communication in PRs, responding to feedback, pairing.
- Bias checks: ensure panel includes at least one non-hiring-manager reviewer; ask the candidate to explain a past small release they owned.
- Decision guidance: hire if average >= 3.5 and no 1s in security or collaboration.

Onboarding artifacts to produce (owner indicated):
- First Release Ticket (manager): concise acceptance criteria, rollback steps, quiet-deployment time.
- Dev runbook snippet (mentor): how to run the target service locally + 3 useful debugging commands.
- Knowledge note (new hire): one-page summary of what they changed and why (to be added to team wiki).
- Quick retrospective note (manager + new hire): what went well, what blocked, follow-ups.

Common friction & mitigation (ops notes):
- Delays in hardware: always ship a temporary cloud dev VM and remote desktop access.
- Access approvals take >48h: pre-raise cloud IAM requests as soon as offer accepted, use emergency dev accounts with strict TTL.
- Overly large first ticket: manager must slice to a clear, testable unit with a rollback.

Measurements (to track for process improvement):
- Time to first green build (target <= 3 days).
- Days to first staging merge (target <= 10 days).
- Number of access-related tickets opened in first 14 days.
- New hire self-reported confidence score on day 14.

Template snippets (copy into PR templates / Jira):
- PR template excerpt: "Assignee: <new hire> | Reviewer: <mentor> | Rollback plan: <one-liner> | Observability: <log/metric added>"
- Ticket acceptance criteria: "1) <change> runs on dev, 2) tests pass, 3) staging smoke run successful, 4) rollback tested or trivial"

Open questions / action items (people-ops owner: Aisha):
- Should we formalize a temporary dev role with a 72h TTL for new hires? (ops cost + security tradeoff).
- Can SRE provide a single-run smoke harness repo for all new joiners? (reduces pairing time).
- Need to draft a short secure-coding checklist tailored to tiny-first-releases (assign to Priya).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep first release intentionally small — psychological wins matter.
- Avoid overloading with too many process items on day 1.
- Add a short checklist card in HR's offer packet so hiring managers complete their side before start.
